  • 铌酸锂薄膜中的局域高Q导模谐振实现电光相位调制，为高速可重构超表面提供新平台

惠更斯超表面赋能的中红外计算光谱仪

Huygens metasurface-enabled mid-wave infrared computational spectrometers
Optics Letters　·　2026-10-15　·　原文链接　·　DOI: 10.1364/ol.614321
论文解决的问题
计算光谱仪受限于光谱编码相关性和重构算法，中红外分子指纹识别需要高性能小型化光谱仪。
核心方法与结构
在CaF2衬底上设计GST纳米盘阵列的惠更斯超表面，利用电偶极与磁偶极谐振的灵活调控实现低相关光谱编码，结合压缩感知算法重构光谱。
关键结果
16个惠更斯超表面的平均相关系数低至0.34，在中红外实现10 nm光谱分辨率，并演示了窄带与宽带吸收谱的重构。
与我们项目的关联
结构设计（惠更斯条件）与表征方法（计算光谱）环节：直接相关，其利用ED/MD谐振调控实现低相关编码，可为我们惠更斯超表面的谐振解耦与光谱表征提供设计范式；同时其计算光谱方法可用于我们单像素电光表征中突破光谱仪分辨率限制。
可借鉴的点
  • ED/MD谐振独立调控实现低相关光谱编码的设计流程，可迁移到我们的TiO2惠更斯元胞
  • 压缩感知重构算法用于从有限光谱偏移中反演相位变化，解决卡点5的光谱分辨率问题
需要注意 / 待验证
GST在可见光吸收较大，需替换为TiO2并重新优化谐振；压缩感知需标定编码矩阵。
建议下一步
在RCWA中扫描TiO2纳米盘的ED/MD谐振位置，构建16个低相关元胞，并用压缩感知算法重构模拟光谱。

查看英文摘要原文

The mid-wave infrared (MWIR) spectrum is critical for environmental monitoring, gas detection, and related fields as it enables the identification of molecular fingerprints. Despite recent unprecedented progress, computational spectrometers are still constrained by system performance, including spectral encoding and reconstruction algorithms. Here, we propose a promising mechanism for low-correlation spectral encoding, enabled by Huygens metasurfaces (HMSs) consisting of germanium-antimony-telluride (GST) nanodisk arrays on a calcium fluoride (CaF 2 ) substrate. Flexible manipulation of electric and magnetic dipole resonances can be realized following Huygens’ principle, leading to an average correlation coefficient as low as 0.34 for 16 HMSs. Together with a compressed sensing algorithm, the proposed HMS-enabled spectrometer can achieve a 10 nm spectral resolution over the MWIR spectrum. Narrow spectra and wide-band absorption spectra have also been successfully demonstrated.

ABSTRACT Optical neural networks face a tradeoff between device footprint and computational expressivity: deep systems are bulky, whereas single‐layer hardware lacks intrinsic depth and native negative‐weight support. We experimentally demonstrate a single‐layer metalens imager with “spatiotemporal intrinsic depth” for equivalent broadband dual‐layer convolution. A polarization‐multiplexed metasurface provides fixed Bessel‐vortex channels ( l = 0 to 3) as the immutable first convolution layer, where the ( l = 0) channel implements a hardware‐native residual connection. A metasurface‐generated 3 × 3 optical vortex matrix forms the second functional layer; time‐sequential liquid‐crystal amplitude modulation delivers tunable positive/negative weights. This temporal encoding solves the optical sign problem and converts fabrication imperfections into compensable biases via in‐situ training. Dynamic manipulation of the Goos-Hänchen (GH) shift is crucial for photonic applications such as information storage and ultrasensitive sensing. However, most previously reported GH shift enhancements rely on resonance effects or quasi-bound states in the continuum (quasi-BICs), which typically require passive adjustment of structural parameters. Herein, we achieve dynamic evolution of BICs by actively adjusting the excitation power density of the pump light incident upon the phase-change materials (PCMs). By regulating the crystalline phase through the excitation power density of the pump light, two off-Γ points, each bearing a −1 topological charge, gradually approach the Γ point carrying a + 1 topological charge and subsequently merge, giving rise to the annihilation of topological charges. Assisted by controllable quasi-BICs with high reflectance, the value of the GH shift can be flexibly controlled. Based on the enhanced GH shifts by quasi-BICs, we further design an ultrasensitive sensor with a sensitivity exceeding 1 × 10 3 λ /RIU, reaching a maximum value of 2.9 × 10 4 λ /RIU. Planar metasurfaces can profoundly control electromagnetic scattering. At microwave frequencies, such devices are typically implemented using multilayer cascades of patterned metallic sheets, whose design often requires time-consuming full-wave optimization. Here, we extend analytical models originally developed for sparse loaded-wire metagratings to accurately describe densely packed Jerusalem-cross meta-atoms embedded in standard printed circuit board (PCB) dielectric stacks. The model captures both near- and far-field coupling within and between layers, enabling efficient prediction of the dual-polarized response. Using this framework, we identify highly transmissive meta-atoms whose phase is controlled by the leg lengths of the Jerusalem crosses (microscopic design stage).
